summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of liver transplant, chronic kidney disease, and recent cholangitis treated with meropenem was readmitted for weakness and two falls following discharge. He attributed his lightheadedness to the switch to ertapenem. Orthostatic vitals were normal, and telemetry showed no arrhythmias. He received a small IV fluid bolus and was evaluated by physical therapy, who recommended a cane and home safety evaluation. Given his clinical improvement and completion of 10 days of IV antibiotics, he was transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin for the remainder of his treatment. Platelet count was elevated but trending down, likely reactive. Liver enzymes and renal function remained stable. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up in the liver clinic and plans for stent removal in six months.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage I through stage IV, or unspecified
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of prostate
Other musculoskeletal symptoms referable to limbs
